newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA AND FINLAND ADD NHL REINFORCEMENTS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA AND FINLAND ADD NHL REINFORCEMENTS.

text.p: Montreal Canadiens centre Saku Koivu led what is expected to become an influx of NHL reinforcements at the world ice hockey championships on Sunday.

While Canada and Finland confirmed they have added players, Russia, the United States, Latvia and Slovakia indicated they were hopeful of filling vacancies as more teams become eliminated from the Stanley Cup playoffs.
Koivu, who scored 17 goals and 56 points in 50 games for the Canadiens this season, is expected to be in Finland's team in time for Tuesday's game against Germany.
Canada bolstered their attack with the addition of Koivu's Canadiens team mate, right winger Mark Recchi, who finished second in team scoring with 34 goals and 80 points.
"We talked to him 10 minutes ago and we're trying to get him on a plane now," said Bob Nicholson, head of the Canadian team delegation. "He'll be here tomorrow."
Canada has one spot on their 23-man roster left to fill but said they would wait until after Sunday's game against Sweden to decide how to fill it.

The Russians confirmed they were hopeful of having Pittsburgh Penguins defenceman Darius Kasparaitis join their team. They have left another spot vacant for Ottawa centre Alexei Yashin, should the Senators be eliminated.

Latvia, who lost their opening game 5-4 to the United States, would also like to see the Senators go out so they could add centre Sergei Zholtok. Dallas Stars goaltender Arturs Irbe also remains on the Latvian wish list.
The American's added minor leaguer Chris Tancill to their line-up for the match against Latvia but coach Jeff Jackson said later that he is holding more places open for NHL help.
"We have three spots open for players to come in during the next few days," said Jackson. "I will say we anticipate using one of those spots to add a goaltender."
